title: Throughput contract orchestrator and hybrid autoscaler for Dedicated fleets
creator: Marco Chen
description: Implement an autoscaling policy engine for Dedicated capacity that enforces per-tenant throughput contracts while optimizing for cost and latency. The engine should produce stable capacity changes, tolerate noisy signals from upstream routing, and gracefully degrade by triggering model-variant fallbacks and rate-limited admission when the fleet cannot meet contracted throughput. This ticket covers metric definitions, the hybrid scaling algorithm design (PID + discrete stepper), safety envelopes, and the operational controls surfaced in the Console.
background: Customers on Dedicated plan expect throughput guarantees for committed units. Current fleet autoscalers are tuned for latency percentiles and node-level CPU/GPU utilization; they do not reason about contract-level throughput or coordinated tenant-level headroom. We also observed oscillation when short-lived bursts hit simple proportional controllers, and insufficient safety limits during instance preemption windows. This work aims to add a contract-oriented control plane that integrates with existing routing and quota subsystems.
proposal: 1) Define the canonical target metric: committed_throughput(tokens_per_sec) per tenant and a secondary soft target for p95 latency. 2) Implement a hybrid controller: a PID loop for continuous small adjustments to preserve stability and a stepper layer that issues discrete scale-out steps when projected shortfall exceeds a configurable headroom threshold. 3) Safety limits: max_scale_rate, surge_credit_bucket, min_stable_window, and backoff_on_failed_provision. 4) Integrate with routing fallback to model variants and admission controls to ensure graceful degradation. 5) Expose controls in Console and a policy DSL for per-tenant overrides.
design_decisions: Use committed_throughput (tokens/sec) as primary control signal rather than raw request rate to better reflect cost and billing implications.
Hybrid algorithm chosen because PID alone was too slow to recover from sudden demand and pure stepper caused oscillations under noisy telemetry.
Surge credits are per-tenant and per-fleet to allow short bursts without immediate permanent scaling; credits decay on fixed half-life to bound debt.
Default max_scale_rate set to 2x capacity per 5 minutes to limit runaway provisioning costs; can be relaxed via customer contracts.
Model-variant fallback is preferred to wholesale admission throttling; admission controls are a last resort to protect other tenants.
Expose policy as a JSON DSL compatible with existing autoscale policies to ease adoption by tooling and infra teams.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can enforce committed_throughput for synthetic tenant workloads in staging for sustained 60m windows with <5% SLA misses.
Scale actions obey configured max_scale_rate and do not exceed surge_credit allocation without explicit override.
When capacity is insufficient, system triggers model-variant fallback and logs a clear event; admission throttling only occurs after fallback exhaustion.
Console shows per-tenant throughput contract usage, surge credit balance, upcoming scale actions, and recent failed provisions with links to logs.
Automated chaos test (simulate instance boot delay and partial provisioning) demonstrates no oscillatory scaling loops over 4 hours.
Unit and integration tests cover PID tuning boundaries, stepper thresholds, and credit accounting edge cases.
tasks: Define metric schemas and ingest pipelines for committed_throughput and projected_shortfall (SLO: 10s compute window).
Implement hybrid controller library in runtime-autoscaler service with feature flag gating.
Add surge credit accounting and API to allocate/consume credits per tenant.
Wire controller events to Console UI and build mini-dashboard for policy observability.
Create policy DSL bindings and update onboarding docs and examples.
Write end-to-end tests and a chaos experiment harness for staged validation.
Run staged rollout: opt-in beta tenants -> internal smoke canary -> broad rollout.
risks: Incorrect headroom projection could cause premature scale-outs, increasing cost for customers.
Surge credit accounting bugs could allow unlimited bursts, breaking commitments to other tenants.
Tight PID gains risk oscillation when telemetry latency spikes; need robust fallback to stepper layer.
Capacity provisioning failures (cloud slow boots or preemption) could cause transient SLA breaches; careful backoff required.
notes: We should coordinate with Billing to ensure committed_throughput aligns with invoiced units. Early experiments show a 12% average cost reduction versus naive step-scaling for spiky workloads when using hybrid approach. Initial PID params in prototype: Kp=0.6, Ki=0.08, Kd=0.03 (subject to tuning).
